security.title: Data Access Operations Outside of Expected Data Manager Component
security.description: The product uses a dedicated, central data manager component as required by design, but it contains code that performs data-access operations that do not use this data manager.

evidence.explanation: Startup.Auth.CreateAdminUser constructs a concrete PartsUnlimitedContext directly when creating the RoleStore, instead of resolving/using the IPartsUnlimitedContext data-manager abstraction used throughout the application. This is a data-access operation outside the established context boundary (line 179).

security.title: Use of Hard-coded Password
security.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

evidence.explanation: The checked-in Web.config defines a nonempty Authentication.Administrator.Password app setting, and Startup.Auth.CreateAdminUser reads that setting to create the built-in administrator account. The credential is therefore a hard-coded password in configuration (Web.config line 12); the literal value is intentionally omitted.

security.title: Insufficient Logging
security.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: AccountController.Login processes password sign-in and branches on the authentication result without recording successful or failed login attempts in an audit/security log (lines 48-57 and subsequent result handling). This leaves authentication events unauditable.

security.title: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
security.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.

evidence.explanation: The checked-in Web.config defines a nonempty Authentication.Administrator.Password app setting, and Startup.Auth.CreateAdminUser reads that setting to create the built-in administrator account. The credential is therefore a hard-coded password in configuration (Web.config line 12); the literal value is intentionally omitted.
